subproblems.title: Push-forward of compactly supported integer multiplicity currents by a map that is C¹ near the support (Simon 6.2.23–2.29, 3.3–3.9)
subproblems.statement:
Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, O ⊆ ℝ^P open, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P C¹ on O (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O). Then there is a map push : 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) → 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with the following properties.
(A) Let Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity with spt Y compact and spt Y ⊆ O, and let (M, θ, ξ) be any integer multiplicity representation of Y. Then:
 (i) push Y(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·⟨ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). Here (ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x))(v₁, …, vₙ) = ω(f(x))(Df(x)v₁, …, Df(x)vₙ); in Lean, (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x).
 (ii) push Y is integer multiplicity.
 (iii) spt push Y ⊆ f(spt Y).
 (iv) For every real L with ‖Df(y)‖ ≤ L for all y ∈ O, M(push Y) ≤ Lⁿ·M(Y), as ENNReal.ofReal (L^n) * M(Y).
 (v) If ∂Y = 0, then ∂(push Y) = 0.
(B) push(Y₁ − Y₂) = push Y₁ − push Y₂ for all integer multiplicity Y₁, Y₂ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with compact supports contained in O.
This is f_#Y of Simon 2.24(2) and 3.9.

Accepted proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, chapter-06.txt lines 404–530 and 770–860, with the area formula of Ch. 3, 2.4–2.6:
 • 2.23–2.24: push-forward and its boundary, and the explicit formula 2.24(2) for currents with locally finite mass and C¹ maps;
 • 2.27–2.29: homotopy estimate and mollified maps;
 • 3.3–3.9: push-forward of integer multiplicity currents by locally Lipschitz maps that are proper on the support; by 3.9, f_#T is integer multiplicity.
This is the result cited as (C3) in step 6 of the parent proof, with the properties listed there. The printed arguments are copied and specialised to a map f that is C¹ on an open set O containing the compact support. Two facts the source uses tacitly are proved in steps 2–3: additivity (B), and independence of the formula from the representation.

Notation. n = m + 1 and Hⁿ = μHE[n]. For an n-covector α and a linear map A, α ∘ ΛⁿA is the covector (v₁, …, vₙ) ↦ α(Av₁, …, Avₙ). For x ∈ O write Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x. 𝒴 is the class of integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with spt Y compact and contained in O. |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm.

1. (Preliminaries.)
 (a) Let v₁, …, vₙ ∈ ℝ^P and let V be the P×n matrix with columns vᵢ. By multilinearity and the alternating property, α(v₁, …, vₙ) = Σ_I α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)})·det(V_I), the sum over strictly increasing I : {1, …, n} → {1, …, P}, where V_I is the n×n submatrix of rows I. By Cauchy–Schwarz, |α(v₁, …, vₙ)| ≤ |α|·(Σ_I det(V_I)²)^{1/2}. By the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I det(V_I)² = det(VᵀV), the Gram determinant, which is at most Π_i|vᵢ|² by Hadamard's inequality. Now let τ₁, …, τₙ be orthonormal, ζ = ±τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τₙ, and vᵢ := Aτᵢ. Then |⟨α ∘ ΛⁿA, ζ⟩| = |α(Aτ₁, …, Aτₙ)| ≤ |α|·Π_i|Aτᵢ| ≤ |α|·‖A‖ⁿ. For n = 0 both sides equal |α|.
 (b) Let Y ∈ 𝒴, K := spt Y, and (M, θ, ξ) a representation of Y. Then Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0. Indeed ℝ^P ∖ K is open and Y vanishes on forms supported there (vanish_off_support), so μ_Y(ℝ^P ∖ K) = M_{ℝ^P∖K}(Y) = 0 (mass_eq_measure), and θ ≥ 1 on M.
 (c) Df is continuous on O ⊇ K, so Λ_K := sup_K ‖Df‖ < ∞. Also μ_Y(K) < ∞ by local finiteness of the weight.

2. (Definition and independence of the representation; Simon 2.24(2), 3.3.)
 (a) For Y ∈ 𝒴 with a representation (M, θ, ξ) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), let I(ω) := ∫_M θ⟨ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x).
 (b) By 1(a)–(c) the integrand is bounded by θ·sup|ω|·Λ_Kⁿ·1_K Hⁿ-a.e. on M. So the integral exists, is linear in ω, and |I(ω)| ≤ sup|ω|·Λ_Kⁿ·μ_Y(K). Hence I is sequentially continuous on test forms (TestFormOnConverges gives uniform convergence) and defines a current.
 (c) I does not depend on the representation. Choose χ ∈ C_c^∞(O) with χ = 1 on a neighbourhood of K, and put β(x) := χ(x)·(ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x)), a continuous compactly supported n-form. By 1(b), I(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨β, ξ⟩ dHⁿ. Mollifying β gives smooth β_k with supports in a fixed compact set and β_k → β uniformly. By dominated convergence ∫_M θ⟨β, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = lim_k ∫_M θ⟨β_k, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = lim_k Y(β_k), which depends only on Y.
 (d) Define push Y := I for Y ∈ 𝒴, and push Y := 0 for Y ∉ 𝒴. Then (i) holds for every representation.

3. ((B) additivity.) Let Y₁, Y₂ ∈ 𝒴 with supports K₁, K₂.
 (a) Y₁ − Y₂ is integer multiplicity (im_calculus (c)). It vanishes on every form whose support misses the compact set K₁ ∪ K₂ ⊆ O (vanish_off_support for Y₁ and Y₂). So spt(Y₁ − Y₂) is compact and contained in K₁ ∪ K₂ (support_of_vanishing), and Y₁ − Y₂ ∈ 𝒴.
 (b) Take χ = 1 near K₁ ∪ K₂ in step 2. Then push(Y₁ − Y₂)(ω) = lim_k (Y₁ − Y₂)(β_k) = lim_k Y₁(β_k) − lim_k Y₂(β_k) = push Y₁(ω) − push Y₂(ω).

4. ((iii) support; Simon 2.29.) Let Y ∈ 𝒴. f(K) is compact, since f is continuous on O ⊇ K. If tsupport ω ∩ f(K) = ∅, then ω(f(x)) = 0 for x ∈ K, so by 1(b) the integrand in (i) vanishes Hⁿ-a.e. on M and push Y(ω) = 0. By support_of_vanishing (with U = ℝ^P and the compact set f(K)), spt push Y ⊆ f(K) = f(spt Y).

5. ((iv) mass; Simon 2.29.) Let L satisfy ‖Df(y)‖ ≤ L for y ∈ O. If O ≠ ∅ then L ≥ 0; if O = ∅ then K = ∅, μ_Y = 0 and push Y = 0. For every admissible ω (|ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y), by 1(a)(b): push Y(ω) ≤ ∫_M θ|ω(f(x))|·‖Df(x)‖ⁿ dHⁿ ≤ Lⁿ∫_M θ dHⁿ = Lⁿ·μ_Y(ℝ^P) = Lⁿ·M(Y), by mass_eq_measure with W = ℝ^P. Taking the supremum, M(push Y) ≤ Lⁿ·M(Y).

6. ((ii) integer multiplicity; Simon 3.5–3.9.) Let Y ∈ 𝒴 with representation (M, θ, ξ). By 1(b) we may replace M by M ∩ K.
 (a) Choose an open V with K ⊆ V and closure(V) ⊆ O compact. Near each point of closure(V), f is C¹ and Lipschitz.
 (b) On M the tangential differential d^M f_x : T_xM → ℝ^P exists Hⁿ-a.e., and d^M f_{x#}ξ(x) = Df(x)_#ξ(x), Df(x) restricted to T_xM (Simon Ch. 3, 2.2). So (i) reads push Y(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω(f(x)), d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ.
 (c) Let M₊ := {x ∈ M : J^M f(x) > 0}. Points with J^M f = 0 contribute nothing, since there d^M f_{x#}ξ(x) = 0 (3.4). Since |d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)| = J^M f(x), the area formula (Ch. 3, 2.5) gives (3.6):
 push Y(ω) = ∫_{f(M₊)} ⟨ω(y), Σ_{x ∈ f⁻¹(y)∩M₊} θ(x) d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)/|d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)|⟩ dHⁿ(y).
 (d) f(M₊) is countably n-rectifiable, as a union of Lipschitz images of the pieces of M on which f is Lipschitz. So for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ f(M₊) the approximate tangent space T_y f(M₊) exists. For Hⁿ-a.e. such y the set f⁻¹(y) ∩ M₊ is finite (2.4), and each vector d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)/|d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)| with x in it equals ±η(y), for a unit simple n-vector η(y) orienting T_y f(M₊) (3.7).
 (e) Hence (3.8) Σ_x θ(x) d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)/|…| = N(y)η(y) with N(y) ∈ ℤ. Replacing η by −η where N < 0, push Y = τ(f(M₊) ∩ {N ≠ 0}, |N|, η) (3.9).
 (f) The multiplicity is locally integrable: ∫_{f(M₊)} |N| dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{f(M₊)} Σ_x θ(x) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_M θ J^M f dHⁿ ≤ Λ_Kⁿ·μ_Y(K) < ∞ (area formula 2.5).
 (g) Choosing Borel versions of the carrier, N and η, this is an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P representing push Y. So push Y is integer multiplicity.

7. ((v) boundary; Simon 2.24(1), 2.29.) Let Y ∈ 𝒴 with ∂Y = 0, and V as in step 6.
 (a) Let χ₁ ∈ C_c^∞(O) with χ₁ = 1 on a neighbourhood of closure(V), and f_σ := (χ₁f) ∗ φ_σ for σ > 0 (mollification). Then f_σ is smooth on ℝ^P, and f_σ → f, Df_σ → Df uniformly on closure(V) as σ ↓ 0, because f is C¹ near closure(V).
 (b) For the smooth map g := f_σ, Simon 2.23 defines g_#Y(ω) := Y(ζ g^#ω) with ζ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P), ζ = 1 near K; the value does not depend on ζ.
 (c) By 2.24(1), ∂g_#Y = g_#∂Y = 0. Indeed ∂g_#Y(ω) = Y(ζ g^#dω) = Y(ζ d(g^#ω)) = Y(d(ζ g^#ω)) − Y(dζ ∧ g^#ω) = (∂Y)(ζ g^#ω) − 0 = 0, because dζ ∧ g^#ω vanishes near K = spt Y.
 (d) By 2.24(2), g_#Y(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω(f_σ(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf_σ(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ. As σ ↓ 0 this tends to push Y(ω), by dominated convergence (uniform convergence on K and the bound of step 2).
 (e) Hence ∂(push Y)(ω) = push Y(dω) = lim_σ f_{σ#}Y(dω) = lim_σ ∂(f_{σ#}Y)(ω) = 0 for every ω. ∎
proof_key_steps: For Y with compact support K ⊆ O, push Y(ω) := ∫_M θ⟨ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ (2.24(2)) is a current. It does not depend on the representation (approximate the continuous form χ·f^#ω by smooth forms), and push Y := 0 otherwise.
Additivity follows from independence of the representation. The support lies in f(K), since the integrand vanishes off f⁻¹(spt ω).
Mass: |⟨α ∘ ΛⁿA, ξ⟩| ≤ |α|·‖A‖ⁿ (Cauchy–Binet, Hadamard) gives M(push Y) ≤ Lⁿ·M(Y).
Integer multiplicity by the area formula: push Y = τ(f(M₊), |N|, ±η) with N integer valued (3.6–3.9).
If ∂Y = 0 then ∂(push Y) = 0: push Y is the weak limit of push-forwards by smooth mollified maps, which commute with ∂ (2.24(1), 2.29).

subproblems.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep: M ⊆ U Borel and countably n-rectifiable, θ : ℝ^P → ℕ measurable with θ ≥ 1 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, ξ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable and, Hⁿ-a.e. on M, equal to ±τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ for an orthonormal basis τ of the approximate tangent space) with T = τ(M, θ, ξ), i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Let μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M (R.measure). Then (i) M_W(T) = μ_R(W) in [0, ∞] for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, where M_W(T) is the supremum of T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; (ii) spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R.

Accepted proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–765: M_W(T) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ for open W) and Ch. 6, 2.11–2.12 (chapter-06.txt lines 295–307: spt T = spt μ_T). The book states both without proof; a complete proof follows. Notation: M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, μ_R = R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M. For an n-covector α, |α| = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm; I runs over strictly increasing multi-indices, e_I = (e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})), and dx^I denotes the coordinate covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ}. ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ means ξ(x)(α).
1. Pointwise algebra. Let x ∈ M be a point where R.orients holds: there are an orthonormal family τ₁, …, τₙ and s ∈ {1, −1} with ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = s·α(τ₁, …, τₙ) for every α. Expanding τ_j = Σ_i τ_j^i e_i, multilinearity and alternation give α(τ₁, …, τₙ) = Σ_I α(e_I)·det(τ^I), where det(τ^I) is the n×n minor of the matrix (τ_j^i) on the rows I; by the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I det(τ^I)² = det(τᵀτ) = 1. By Cauchy–Schwarz, |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for every α. The covector ξ^♭(x) := Σ_I ⟨dx^I, ξ(x)⟩ dx^I has coefficients s·det(τ^I), hence |ξ^♭(x)| = 1 and ⟨ξ^♭(x), ξ(x)⟩ = Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1. (For n = 0 the only I is empty: |α| = |α()|, ξ(x) = ±evaluation, ξ^♭(x) = ±1.) Since R.orients holds Hⁿ-a.e. on M and μ_R ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, these facts hold μ_R-a.e. The field x ↦ ξ^♭(x) is μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable, being a continuous linear function of the a.e. strongly measurable ξ (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient).
2. Integral formula. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the function x ↦ θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable: it is a.e. strongly measurable, vanishes off the compact set spt ω ⊆ U, is bounded by θ·sup|ω| a.e. (step 1), and ∫_{M∩spt ω} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult). Hence T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R (integral with respect to the density θ).
3. Upper bound. Let W be open and ω admissible for M_W(T) (ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), spt ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x). By step 1, ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for μ_R-a.e. x, and ω = 0 off W, so T(ω) ≤ μ_R(W) by step 2. Taking the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
4. Lower bound. Let W be open and t a real number with t < μ_R(W); we construct an admissible ω with T(ω) > t, which proves M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(W) (also when μ_R(W) = ∞). Put G := W ∩ U (open). Since M ⊆ U, μ_R(G) = μ_R(W). μ_R is a Borel measure, finite on compact subsets of U; restricted to the open σ-compact set G it is a Radon measure (Simon Ch. 1, 1.15), hence inner regular by compact sets and outer regular on sets of finite measure. Fix η > 0 and a compact K ⊆ G with μ_R(K) > t + 4η. (a) Lusin (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17): there is a compact K' ⊆ K with μ_R(K ∖ K') < η such that ξ^♭ restricted to K' is continuous, and |ξ^♭| = 1, ⟨ξ^♭, ξ⟩ = 1 μ_R-a.e. on K'. (b) There is an open V with K' ⊆ V, V̄ compact, V̄ ⊆ G, and μ_R(V ∖ K') < η. (c) Extend the coefficients of ξ^♭ on K' continuously to ℝ^P (Tietze), compose with the radial retraction of Λⁿ(ℝ^P) onto its closed unit ball for |·|, and multiply by a continuous χ with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on K', spt χ ⊆ V. The resulting continuous g has compact support in V, |g| ≤ 1 everywhere and g = ξ^♭ on K'. (d) Let g_ε := φ_ε ∗ g (coefficientwise convolution with a standard mollifier). For 0 < ε < dist(spt g, ℝ^P ∖ V), g_ε is C^∞ with compact support in V ⊆ W ∩ U, |g_ε(x)| ≤ ∫ φ_ε(x − y)|g(y)| dy ≤ 1 by convexity of the norm, and g_ε → g uniformly as ε → 0; so g_ε is admissible for M_W(T). (e) By steps 2 and 1, T(g_ε) = ∫⟨g_ε, ξ⟩ dμ_R ≥ ∫_{K'}⟨g, ξ⟩ dμ_R − ∫_{V∖K'}|⟨g, ξ⟩| dμ_R − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) ≥ μ_R(K') − η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) ≥ μ_R(K) − 2η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) > t + 2η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄). As μ_R(V̄) < ∞, T(g_ε) > t for small ε. Together with step 3 this proves (i): M_W(T) = μ_R(W).
5. Support. By definition (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.support; Simon 2.11) spt T = U ∖ Z, where Z is the union of all open W with W̄ compact, W̄ ⊆ U and T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ W. Recall x ∈ spt μ_R iff μ_R(B) > 0 for every neighbourhood B of x. (a) If x ∈ U ∩ spt μ_R and x ∈ Z, choose W in the union with x ∈ W; every admissible form for M_W(T) has T(ω) = 0, so M_W(T) = 0, hence μ_R(W) = 0 by (i), contradicting x ∈ spt μ_R. So U ∩ spt μ_R ⊆ spt T. (b) spt T ⊆ U by definition. If x ∈ U ∖ spt μ_R, choose r > 0 with μ_R(B_r(x)) = 0 and B̄_r(x) ⊆ U (U open). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ B_r(x), T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R = 0 by step 2; so B_r(x) is one of the sets forming Z, x ∈ Z and x ∉ spt T. Hence spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R, which is (ii).
proof_key_steps: For a unit simple n-vector ξ, |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α| (Cauchy–Binet), with equality for the dual covector ξ^♭.
T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R, so admissible forms give T(ω) ≤ μ_R(W).
Lusin, Tietze extension, retraction and mollification of ξ^♭ give admissible forms with T(ω) arbitrarily close to μ_R(W).
The mass formula identifies the zero region of T with the complement of spt μ_R in U.

Accepted proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(1) (chapter-06.txt lines 755–756, stated without proof). Tools: the Upper Density Theorem, Ch. 1, 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2) (chapter-01.txt lines 700–722; SimonGMT Chapter01/DensityComparison.lean), and the fact that approximate tangent spaces only depend on a set up to sets of zero density, Ch. 3, 1.4–1.5 and Remark 1.8(1) (chapter-03.txt lines 77–108, 298–310). Throughout Hⁿ = μHE[n], η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap), and Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(E)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(E) for all E (μHE[n] is translation invariant and n-homogeneous: Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). Let R₁ = (M₁, θ₁, ξ₁) and R₂ = (M₂, θ₂, ξ₂) be IMReps in U representing S and T.
1. Local finiteness. For compact K ⊆ U, Hⁿ(M_i ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M_i∩K} θ_i dHⁿ < ∞ since θ_i ≥ 1 on M_i. Hence every Borel A ⊆ M₁ ∪ M₂ has Hⁿ(A ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U.
2. (F1) If A ⊆ M₁ ∪ M₂ is Borel, then ρ^{−n}Hⁿ(A ∩ B_ρ(y)) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0 for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ U ∖ A. Proof: let V_j be open sets with compact closures in U and ⋃_j V_j = U; apply Ch. 1, 3.6 to the finite Borel-regular measure Hⁿ⌞(A ∩ V_j) to get the conclusion for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ V_j ∖ A (for y ∈ V_j and small ρ, B_ρ(y) ⊆ V_j), and take the union of the countably many exceptional null sets.
3. (F2) Let A, A' be Hⁿ-measurable, y ∈ U, s > 0 with Hⁿ(A ∩ B_s(y)), Hⁿ(A' ∩ B_s(y)) < ∞, ρ^{−n}Hⁿ((A Δ A') ∩ B_ρ(y)) → 0, and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A y Q. Then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A' y Q. Proof: finrank Q = n is unchanged. For f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_L(0) and 0 < r < s/L both blow-up integrals are finite and |∫_{η_{y,r}(A')} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{y,r}(A)} f dHⁿ| ≤ sup|f|·Hⁿ(η_{y,r}(A Δ A') ∩ B_L(0)) = sup|f|·r^{−n}Hⁿ((A Δ A') ∩ B_{Lr}(y)) → 0, so the blow-up integrals of A' converge to ∫_Q f dHⁿ as well.
4. (F3) If ζ and ζ' are both unit orientations of the same n-dimensional subspace Q (IsUnitOrientationOf), then ζ' = ±ζ: if ζ(α) = σα(τ) and ζ'(α) = σ'α(τ') with τ, τ' orthonormal bases of Q, then τ' = τB for an orthogonal n×n matrix B, and multilinearity plus the alternating property give α(τ') = det(B)α(τ) with det B = ±1.
5. Normalization. Changing ξ_i on an Hⁿ⌞M_i-null set changes neither the integrals in R_i.Represents nor the almost-everywhere statement `orients`; so we may assume ξ₁, ξ₂ Borel measurable. Put E := M₁ ∩ M₂. For increasing I : {1,…,n} → {1,…,P} let e^I ∈ Λⁿ(ℝ^P) be the covector e^I(v₁,…,vₙ) = det(⟨e_{I(a)}, v_b⟩)_{a,b}; these form a basis of Λⁿ(ℝ^P), so an n-vector ζ (a linear functional on Λⁿ) is determined by the numbers ζ(e^I). If ζ(α) = ±α(τ) for an orthonormal frame τ, then ζ ≠ 0 (the covector (v₁,…,vₙ) ↦ det(⟨τ_a, v_b⟩) takes the value ±1 under ζ), hence Σ_I ζ(e^I)² > 0.
6. Common tangent planes. For Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M_i the approximate tangent space T_yM_i exists and ξ_i(y) orients it. By F1 (with A = M₁ ∖ M₂ and A = M₂ ∖ M₁) and F2 (with A = M_i, A' = E, since M_i Δ E ⊆ M₁ ∖ M₂ or ⊆ M₂ ∖ M₁ and y ∉ these sets), for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ E the space T_yE exists and T_yM₁ = T_yE = T_yM₂. By F3, for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ E, ξ₂(y) = σ'ξ₁(y) for some σ' ∈ {±1}; then Σ_I ξ₁(y)(e^I)ξ₂(y)(e^I) = σ'Σ_I ξ₁(y)(e^I)² with Σ_I ξ₁(y)(e^I)² > 0 (step 5), so σ' = σ(y) := sign(Σ_I ξ₁(y)(e^I)·ξ₂(y)(e^I)), a Borel function, and ξ₂(y) = σ(y)ξ₁(y). The set of points of E where any of these properties fails is Hⁿ-null, hence contained in a Borel null set; let G ⊆ E be the Borel complement of that null set in E.
7. New data. On G put d := θ₁ − σθ₂ ∈ ℤ and G' := {y ∈ G : d(y) ≠ 0}. Define the Borel set M := (M₁ ∖ M₂) ∪ (M₂ ∖ M₁) ∪ G', the measurable m : ℝ^P → ℕ with m = θ₁ on M₁ ∖ M₂, m = θ₂ on M₂ ∖ M₁, m = |d| on G', m = 0 elsewhere, and the Borel ζ with ζ = ξ₁ on M₁ ∖ M₂, ζ = −ξ₂ on M₂ ∖ M₁, ζ = sign(d)ξ₁ on G', ζ = 0 elsewhere.
8. IMRep fields. M ⊆ M₁ ∪ M₂ ⊆ U; M is countably n-rectifiable (subset of the union of two countably n-rectifiable sets: SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable.mono, countablyRectifiable_iUnion); m ≥ 1 on M; m ≤ θ₁1_{M₁} + θ₂1_{M₂} (on G', |d| ≤ θ₁ + θ₂), so ∫_{M∩K} m dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M₁∩K} θ₁ + ∫_{M₂∩K} θ₂ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; ζ is Borel, hence a.e. strongly measurable. Orientation property for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M: (i) y ∈ M₁ ∖ M₂: M Δ M₁ ⊆ M₂ and, by F1 with A = M₂, M₂ has density 0 at a.e. y ∉ M₂, so F2 gives T_yM = T_yM₁, oriented by ξ₁(y) = ζ(y); (ii) y ∈ M₂ ∖ M₁: symmetrically T_yM = T_yM₂, oriented by ξ₂(y) and hence by ζ(y) = −ξ₂(y) (IsUnitOrientationOf allows either sign); (iii) y ∈ G': M Δ M₁ = (M₂ ∖ M₁) ∪ (E ∖ G') is a Borel set not containing y, so by F1 it has density 0 at a.e. such y, and F2 gives T_yM = T_yM₁, oriented by ξ₁(y) and hence by ζ(y) = ±ξ₁(y).
9. Representation. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (all integrands are integrable, being bounded by (θ₁1_{M₁} + θ₂1_{M₂})·sup|ω|·1_{tsupport ω}): (S − T)(ω) = ∫_{M₁}θ₁ξ₁(ω) − ∫_{M₂}θ₂ξ₂(ω) = ∫_{M₁∖M₂}θ₁ξ₁(ω) + ∫_{M₂∖M₁}θ₂(−ξ₂)(ω) + ∫_E (θ₁ξ₁ − θ₂ξ₂)(ω) dHⁿ. On G, θ₁ξ₁ − θ₂ξ₂ = (θ₁ − σθ₂)ξ₁ = |d|·sign(d)ξ₁, which vanishes on G ∖ G', and E ∖ G is Hⁿ-null; so the last integral equals ∫_{G'} |d| sign(d)ξ₁(ω) dHⁿ. Hence (S − T)(ω) = ∫_M m ζ(ω) dHⁿ, i.e. (M, m, ζ) is an IMRep in U representing S − T, and S − T is integer multiplicity.
proof_key_steps: Upper Density Theorem: a set of locally finite Hⁿ-measure has density zero at Hⁿ-a.e. point outside it.
Approximate tangent spaces are unchanged by modifications of density zero, so on M₁ ∩ M₂ the tangent planes agree a.e. and ξ₂ = ±ξ₁.
Combine carriers: M₁∖M₂, M₂∖M₁ and the part of M₁∩M₂ where θ₁ξ₁ ≠ θ₂ξ₂, with integer multiplicities |θ₁ ∓ θ₂| and signed orientations.
Verify every IMRep field and the representation identity for S − T.

Accepted proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 (definition of spt T, chapter-06.txt lines 297–301); the partition-of-unity argument below is the standard reason why the union in 2.11 is itself a set on which the current vanishes. Notation: "S vanishes on W" means S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W.
1. K := tsupport ω is compact and K ⊆ U, because ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is a compactly supported smooth form with tsupport ω ⊆ U. If K = ∅ then ω = 0 and S(ω) = 0 by linearity; assume K ≠ ∅.
2. Since K ⊆ U and K ∩ spt S = ∅, we have K ⊆ U ∖ spt S ⊆ Z_S. By compactness there are finitely many open sets W₁,…,W_m from the family defining Z_S (each with S vanishing on W_i) such that K ⊆ W₁ ∪ … ∪ W_m.
3. Take a smooth partition of unity on ℝ^P subordinate to the open cover {W₁,…,W_m, ℝ^P ∖ K} (e.g. Mathlib's SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate for the closed set K and the cover by W₁,…,W_m): smooth ψ₁,…,ψ_m : ℝ^P → [0,1] with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i for each i and Σ_i ψ_i(y) = 1 for every y ∈ K.
4. For each i, ψ_iω (pointwise product of a smooth function and a smooth n-form) is smooth, and tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ tsupport ψ_i ∩ tsupport ω ⊆ W_i ∩ K; in particular it is compact and contained in U. Thus ψ_iω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ W_i, and S(ψ_iω) = 0 since S vanishes on W_i.
5. ω = Σ_i ψ_iω pointwise: if ω(y) ≠ 0 then y ∈ K and Σ_iψ_i(y) = 1; if ω(y) = 0 both sides vanish. By linearity of S, S(ω) = Σ_i S(ψ_iω) = 0.
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω is a compact subset of the zero region of S, hence covered by finitely many open sets on which S vanishes.
A smooth partition of unity subordinate to this finite cover splits ω into test forms supported in those sets.
Each piece is annihilated by S; linearity gives S(ω) = 0.

Use in the selected node: sibling projected_mass (its step 4) builds a representation R of T + X (= S in the parent) whose vector density is 1_{M_T}θ_Tξ_T + 1_{M_X}θ_Xξ_X a.e.; this makes the action additive on the non-compactly supported forms q^#ω (supplied step 4). The sibling names cited in the accepted proof below are the accepted prerequisites of that node in its own branch: overlap_orientation_sign = Submission.rsdic_imrep_ae_orient_eq_or_eq_neg_inter and imrep_tangent_transfer = Submission.rsdic_imrep_ae_tangent_orient_of_subset (both accepted with candidate commits in dag.json). Accepted proof:
Source: steps 3–5 of the parent proof. Notation: μ := μHE[n]; M_i := R_i.carrier, θ_i := R_i.mult, ξ_i := R_i.orient; A := M₁ ∪ M₂, a Borel subset of U; sgn : ℤ → {−1, 0, 1} is the sign; for an integer c, |c| ∈ ℕ is its absolute value. For compact K ⊆ U, μ(M_i ∩ K) ≤ ∫⁻_{M_i∩K} θ_i dμ < ∞, because θ_i ≥ 1 on M_i (mult_pos) and by locallyIntegrable_mult.

1. Borel orientations. ξ_i is AEStronglyMeasurable for μ⌞M_i, so there is a strongly measurable (Borel) ξ̃_i : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) with ξ̃_i = ξ_i μ⌞M_i-a.e. (Mathlib AEStronglyMeasurable.mk / ae_eq_mk). Equivalently: for μ-a.e. x, x ∈ M_i ⇒ ξ̃_i(x) = ξ_i(x).

2. Borel sign on the overlap. Define σ(x) := 1 if ξ̃₂(x) = ξ̃₁(x) and σ(x) := −1 otherwise. The set {ξ̃₂ = ξ̃₁} is Borel (both maps are strongly measurable into the metrizable space Λ_n(ℝ^P)), so σ : ℝ^P → ℤ is Borel. Claim: for μ-a.e. x, x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ ⇒ ξ̃₂(x) = σ(x)ξ̃₁(x). Indeed, by the sibling lemma overlap_orientation_sign and step 1, for μ⌞(M₁ ∩ M₂)-a.e. x we have ξ̃₁(x) = ξ₁(x), ξ̃₂(x) = ξ₂(x) and ξ₂(x) = ±ξ₁(x), hence ξ̃₂(x) = ξ̃₁(x) or ξ̃₂(x) = −ξ̃₁(x). In the first case σ(x) = 1; in the second case, if ξ̃₂(x) ≠ ξ̃₁(x) then σ(x) = −1 and ξ̃₂(x) = −ξ̃₁(x), while if ξ̃₂(x) = ξ̃₁(x) we are in the first case. In all cases ξ̃₂(x) = σ(x)ξ̃₁(x). (This equality test replaces the parent proof's coordinate test Σ_I⟨e^I, ξ₁⟩⟨e^I, ξ₂⟩ ≥ 0, whose verification needs the Cauchy–Binet identity; only the property ξ̃₂ = σξ̃₁ a.e. on M₁ ∩ M₂ is used below.)

3. Coefficient and orientation field. Define c : ℝ^P → ℤ and ζ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) by
   c(x) := p₁θ₁(x)1_{M₁}(x) + p₂θ₂(x)(σ(x)1_{M₁∩M₂}(x) + 1_{M₂∖M₁}(x)),   ζ(x) := ξ̃₁(x) if x ∈ M₁, ζ(x) := ξ̃₂(x) otherwise.
c is Borel (ℤ is countable with the discrete σ-algebra; c is built from the Borel maps θ₁, θ₂, σ and the indicators of the Borel sets M₁, M₂), ζ is strongly measurable (piecewise on the Borel set M₁), c = 0 off A, and since at most one of 1_{M₁∩M₂}(x), 1_{M₂∖M₁}(x) is nonzero and |σ| = 1,
   (3a) |c(x)| ≤ |p₁|θ₁(x)1_{M₁}(x) + |p₂|θ₂(x)1_{M₂}(x) for all x.

4. Pointwise identity. Let x satisfy [x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ ⇒ ξ̃₂(x) = σ(x)ξ̃₁(x)]. Then p₁1_{M₁}(x)θ₁(x)ξ̃₁(x) + p₂1_{M₂}(x)θ₂(x)ξ̃₂(x) = c(x)ζ(x). Cases: if x ∉ A both sides are 0; if x ∈ M₁ ∖ M₂ both sides equal p₁θ₁(x)ξ̃₁(x); if x ∈ M₂ ∖ M₁ both sides equal p₂θ₂(x)ξ̃₂(x); if x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ the left side is p₁θ₁(x)ξ̃₁(x) + p₂θ₂(x)σ(x)ξ̃₁(x) = (p₁θ₁(x) + p₂θ₂(x)σ(x))ξ̃₁(x) = c(x)ζ(x).

5. Definition of R. Let M' := {x ∈ A : c(x) ≠ 0}, θ'(x) := |c(x)| ∈ ℕ and ξ'(x) := sgn(c(x))·ζ(x). Since |c|·sgn(c) = c, and c(x) = 0 whenever x ∉ M' (either x ∉ A, or x ∈ A with c(x) = 0), we have
   (5a) 1_{M'}(x)θ'(x)ξ'(x) = c(x)ζ(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P.

6. R = (M', θ', ξ') is an IMRep in U:
   (a) M' is Borel (A and c are Borel) and M' ⊆ A ⊆ U.
   (b) M₁ ∪ M₂ is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_iUnion applied to the sequence M₁, M₂, M₂, …), hence so is M' ⊆ M₁ ∪ M₂ (CountablyRectifiable.mono).
   (c) θ' = |c| is Borel and θ' ≥ 1 on M'.
   (d) For compact K ⊆ U, by (3a): ∫⁻_{M'∩K} θ' dμ ≤ |p₁|∫⁻_{M₁∩K} θ₁ dμ + |p₂|∫⁻_{M₂∩K} θ₂ dμ < ∞.
   (e) ξ' is strongly measurable (product of the Borel real function sgn∘c and ζ), hence AEStronglyMeasurable for μ⌞M'.
   (f) Orientation. M' is Borel, M' ⊆ U, and μ(M' ∩ K) ≤ μ(M₁ ∩ K) + μ(M₂ ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U. subproblems.title: Unit orientations under linear maps: |ξ(α∘L)| ≤ |α|_E·‖L‖ⁿ, and invariance when L fixes the oriented plane
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Q ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace, ξ an n-vector (MultiVector P n, a continuous linear functional on n-covectors) that is a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q: there are an orthonormal family τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) with span τ = Q and a sign s ∈ {1, −1} such that ξ(β) = s·β(τ₁, …, τₙ) for every n-covector β), and L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P a continuous linear map. For an n-covector α let α∘L be the n-covector (v₁, …, vₙ) ↦ α(Lv₁, …, Lvₙ) (α.compContinuousLinearMap L). Then (a) |ξ(α∘L)| ≤ |α|_E·‖L‖ⁿ for every n-covector α, where |·|_E is the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm) and ‖L‖ the operator norm; and (b) if Lv = v for every v ∈ Q, then ξ(α∘L) = ξ(α) for every n-covector α.

Source: step 1(a) of the parent proof (Cauchy–Binet, Cauchy–Schwarz and Hadamard; this is the pointwise estimate behind Simon Ch. 6, 2.27 and 2.29, chapter-06.txt lines 464–520, with Simon's Euclidean norm of 1.15). Notation: e₁, …, e_P the standard basis of ℝ^P. For an n-covector α and a strictly increasing I : {1, …, n} → {1, …, P}, α(e_I) := α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}); |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2}. ‖L‖ is the operator norm. α∘L := α.compContinuousLinearMap L, so (α∘L)(v₁, …, vₙ) = α(Lv₁, …, Lvₙ). For v = (v₁, …, vₙ) in ℝ^P let V be the P×n matrix with entries V_{ij} = ⟨e_i, v_j⟩, V_I its n×n submatrix on the rows I(1), …, I(n), and Γ(v) := det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} = det(VᵀV).
1. Expansion. Writing v_j = Σ_i V_{ij}e_i and expanding by multilinearity, α(v₁, …, vₙ) = Σ_{k : {1..n}→{1..P}} (Π_j V_{k(j)j})·α(e_{k(1)}, …, e_{k(n)}). Terms with k not injective vanish because α is alternating. Each injective k is uniquely I∘σ with I increasing and σ a permutation of {1, …, n}, and α(e_{I∘σ}) = sgn(σ)α(e_I). Grouping, α(v) = Σ_I α(e_I)·Σ_σ sgn(σ)Π_j V_{I(σ(j)),j} = Σ_I α(e_I)·det(V_I).
2. Cauchy–Schwarz. |α(v)| ≤ (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2}(Σ_I det(V_I)²)^{1/2} = |α|_E·(Σ_I det(V_I)²)^{1/2}.
3. Cauchy–Binet. Σ_I det(V_I)² = det(VᵀV) = Γ(v). Proof: det(VᵀV) is multilinear and alternating in the columns of the right factor V; expanding these columns in the standard basis exactly as in step 1 gives det(VᵀV) = Σ_I det((Vᵀ)^I)·det(V_I), where (Vᵀ)^I is the n×n submatrix of Vᵀ on the columns I, i.e. (V_I)ᵀ; so det(VᵀV) = Σ_I det(V_I)². Hence Γ(v) ≥ 0 and |α(v)| ≤ |α|_E·Γ(v)^{1/2}. (This is also the first part of the accepted declaration covectorEuclideanNorm_gram_bounds.)
4. Hadamard. Γ(v) ≤ Π_j |v_j|². If v₁, …, vₙ are linearly dependent, Vc = 0 for some c ≠ 0, so (VᵀV)c = 0 and Γ(v) = 0. Otherwise let σ₁, …, σₙ be the Gram–Schmidt orthonormalization of v₁, …, vₙ: v_j = Σ_{i≤j} T_{ij}σ_i with T upper triangular and T_{jj} = dist(v_j, span(v₁, …, v_{j−1})) ∈ (0, |v_j|]. Then ⟨v_i, v_j⟩ = (TᵀT)_{ij}, so Γ(v) = det(T)² = Π_j T_{jj}² ≤ Π_j |v_j|².
5. Set-up. By IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q there are an orthonormal family τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) with span τ = Q and a sign s ∈ {1, −1} such that ξ(β) = s·β(τ₁, …, τₙ) for every n-covector β.
6. Part (a). Let α be an n-covector. Then ξ(α∘L) = s·(α∘L)(τ) = s·α(Lτ₁, …, Lτₙ). By steps 3 and 4 with v_j := Lτ_j, |ξ(α∘L)| = |α(Lτ₁, …, Lτₙ)| ≤ |α|_E·Γ(Lτ)^{1/2} ≤ |α|_E·Π_j|Lτ_j| ≤ |α|_E·Π_j ‖L‖·|τ_j| = |α|_E·‖L‖ⁿ, since |τ_j| = 1. (For n = 0 all products are empty, the empty I is the only increasing index, |α|_E = |α()| and ξ(α∘L) = s·(α∘L)() = s·α(): the inequality holds with equality.)
7. Part (b). Suppose Lv = v for every v ∈ Q. Each τ_j lies in span τ = Q, so Lτ_j = τ_j and (α∘L)(τ) = α(Lτ₁, …, Lτₙ) = α(τ₁, …, τₙ). Hence ξ(α∘L) = s·α(τ) = ξ(α) for every n-covector α. ∎
proof_key_steps: Expansion α(v) = Σ_I α(e_I)det(V_I) by multilinearity and the alternating property.
Cauchy–Schwarz and Cauchy–Binet: |α(v)| ≤ |α|_E·det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩)^{1/2}.
Hadamard (Gram–Schmidt): det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩) ≤ Π_j|v_j|²; with v_j = Lτ_j this gives |ξ(α∘L)| ≤ |α|_E‖L‖ⁿ.
If L fixes Q pointwise then L fixes each τ_j, so ξ(α∘L) = ±α(τ) = ξ(α).

subproblems.title: Integrability and sup-norm estimate for the IMRep pairing with a bounded, compactly supported covector field

Let F : ℝ^P → Covector(ℝ^P, n) be a.e. strongly measurable for μ := Hⁿ⌞M (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), with F(x) = 0 for all x ∉ C and ‖F(x)‖ ≤ B for all x. Then x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(F(x)) is μ-integrable, and |∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(F(x)) dHⁿ(x)| ≤ B · (∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dHⁿ).toReal.

9. Estimate. By definition of the set integral, ∫_M θ ξ(F) dμHE[n] = ∫ h dμ. Then |∫ h dμ| = ‖∫ h dμ‖ ≤ ∫ g dμ (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, using integrability of g and step 6). By step 8 this gives |∫_M θ ξ(F) dμHE[n]| ≤ B·(∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dμHE[n]).toReal, the second conjunct.

subproblems.title: An approximate tangent plane of M lies in every subspace along which a set carrying H^n-almost all of M is flat
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and M, N ⊆ ℝ^P with H^n(M ∖ N) = 0, where H^n = μHE[n] is the normalized n-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure. No measurability of M or N is assumed. Let x ∈ ℝ^P, and let Q, T be linear subspaces of ℝ^P. Suppose N is flat at x along T: for every real ε > 0 there is a real ρ > 0 such that every z ∈ N with |z − x| < ρ admits some t ∈ T with |z − x − t| ≤ ε|z − x|. Suppose Q is an approximate tangent space of M at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q). That is, finrank Q = n, and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r ↓ 0 (along 𝓝[>] 0), where η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x). Then Q ⊆ T, i.e. Q ≤ T as submodules. Norms and distances are Euclidean.

Reuse note (context, not part of the numbered proof): this child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.atsm_approxTangent_le_of_flat of DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.approx_tangent_in_submanifold-a1.approx_tangent_le_flat-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 038573e401c107149b7c1ae80dd1bc7621b035f5). Its frozen type is byte-identical to the lean_statement above, so the controller reuses that node and creates no new node. Use in the selected node: sibling projection_invariance (its step 3) applies it with N = T = V: a carrier with H^m(M ∖ V) = 0 has all its approximate tangent planes at points x ∈ V inside V (supplied step 1: 'an approximate tangent plane of a subset of V lies in V').

Accepted proof:
Source: steps 3–6 of the parent-supplied proof of approxTangent_le_submanifold_tangentSpace. The flatness established in its step 2 is now a hypothesis, T is an arbitrary linear subspace, and x need not lie in N. Book: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 and Remark 1.5(1) (local book/chapter-03.txt lines 77–86). The resulting inclusion T_xM ⊆ T_xN is used in Ch. 4, 2.6–2.7 (book/chapter-04.txt lines 175–209).
Notation: H^n := μHE[n]. η_r(y) := r⁻¹(y − x), which is Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r y. |·| is the Euclidean norm. B(a, s) and B̄(a, s) are the open and closed balls. dist(q, T) := inf over t ∈ T of |q − t| (Metric.infDist q T).
1. Set-up for contradiction. Let q ∈ Q; we show q ∈ T. Suppose q ∉ T. T is a finite-dimensional linear subspace of ℝ^P, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional), and it is nonempty since 0 ∈ T. Therefore δ := dist(q, T) > 0 (IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos).
2. Test function. Let g(y) := max(0, δ/2 − |y − q|).
- g is continuous and g ≥ 0.
- If g(y) ≠ 0 then |y − q| < δ/2; otherwise δ/2 − |y − q| ≤ 0 and g(y) = 0. Conversely, |y − q| < δ/2 implies g(y) > 0.
- Hence g vanishes outside the compact ball B̄(q, δ/2), so g has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro).
- So g defines f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), the CompactlySupportedContinuousMap ⟨⟨g, continuity⟩, compact support⟩, with f(y) = g(y) for all y.
The parent normalizes |q| = 1 and uses ε = δ/8 and r < ρ/2. Here no normalization is made and the constants of step 4 are used instead; the mathematics is the same.
3. ∫_Q g dH^n > 0. By hypothesis finrank Q = n.
(a) The measure H^n⌞Q is regular (SimonGMT Chapter03 regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule), in particular finite on compact sets. So the continuous, compactly supported g is H^n⌞Q-integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport).
(b) The support of the measure H^n⌞Q is exactly Q (SimonGMT support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule). Since q ∈ Q and B(q, δ/2) is a neighbourhood of q, (H^n⌞Q)(B(q, δ/2)) > 0 (Measure.mem_support_iff_forall, whose explicit argument is the point q).
(c) B(q, δ/2) ⊆ {g ≠ 0}, so (H^n⌞Q)({g ≠ 0}) > 0. Since g ≥ 0 is integrable, ∫_Q g dH^n > 0 (integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg).
4. Constants. |q| + δ > 0. Put ε := δ/(2(|q| + δ)) > 0, so that ε(|q| + δ) = δ/2. Let ρ > 0 be given by the flatness hypothesis for this ε: every z ∈ N with |z − x| < ρ admits t ∈ T with |z − x − t| ≤ ε|z − x|.
5. Vanishing of the blow-up integrals. Fix r with 0 < r < ρ/(|q| + δ). We show ∫_{η_r(M)} g dH^n = 0.
(a) H^n(η_r(M ∖ N)) = 0.
- η_r(M ∖ N) = r⁻¹·A, where A := {y − x : y ∈ M ∖ N} (Set.image_smul, Set.image_image).
- The translation y ↦ y − x is an isometry (dist_sub_right), so H^n(A) = H^n(M ∖ N) = 0 (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image).
- Since r⁻¹ ≠ 0, H^n(r⁻¹·A) = |r⁻¹|^n·H^n(A) = 0 (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀).
(b) {g ≠ 0} ∩ η_r(M) ⊆ η_r(M ∖ N). Let y = η_r(z) with z ∈ M and g(y) ≠ 0; it suffices to show z ∉ N. Suppose z ∈ N.
- By step 2, |y − q| < δ/2, so |y| ≤ |y − q| + |q| < |q| + δ/2.
- Since r ≠ 0, z − x = r·y. Hence |z − x| = r|y| ≤ r(|q| + δ) < ρ.
- By step 4 there is t ∈ T with |z − x − t| ≤ ε|z − x|.
- Then r⁻¹t ∈ T and y − r⁻¹t = r⁻¹(z − x − t). So |y − r⁻¹t| ≤ r⁻¹ε|z − x| = ε|y| ≤ ε(|q| + δ) = δ/2.
- Consequently δ = dist(q, T) ≤ |q − r⁻¹t| ≤ |q − y| + |y − r⁻¹t| < δ/2 + δ/2 = δ (infDist_le_dist_of_mem), a contradiction.
(c) {g ≠ 0} is open because g is continuous, hence Borel.
- By Measure.restrict_apply, which needs measurability only of {g ≠ 0} and not of η_r(M): (H^n⌞η_r(M))({g ≠ 0}) = H^n({g ≠ 0} ∩ η_r(M)).
- By (b) and (a), this is ≤ H^n(η_r(M ∖ N)) = 0 (measure_mono_null).
- So g = 0 almost everywhere for H^n⌞η_r(M) (ae_iff), and ∫_{η_r(M)} g dH^n = 0 (integral_eq_zero_of_ae).
6. Conclusion.
- Apply the hypothesis HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q to f: the function r ↦ ∫_{η_r(M)} g dH^n tends to ∫_Q g dH^n along 𝓝[>] 0.
- The interval (0, ρ/(|q| + δ)) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). So by step 5 this function is eventually 0 along 𝓝[>] 0, and therefore also tends to 0 (Tendsto.congr').
- Since 𝓝[>] 0 is a nontrivial filter on ℝ, limits are unique (tendsto_nhds_unique). Hence ∫_Q g dH^n = 0, contradicting step 3.
- Therefore q ∈ T. As q ∈ Q was arbitrary, Q ≤ T.
(The accepted node's handoff also carries a verified Lean script for this exact statement; it is omitted here because the numbered proof above is complete.)
proof_key_steps: If q ∈ Q ∖ T, then δ = dist(q, T) > 0 because T is closed. The bump g = max(0, δ/2 − |· − q|) lies in C_c and has ∫_Q g dH^n > 0, because spt(H^n⌞Q) = Q and H^n⌞Q is finite on compact sets (finrank Q = n).
The blow-up η_{x,r}(M ∖ N) is H^n-null: H^n is translation invariant and scales by |r⁻¹|^n.

Take ε = δ/(2(|q| + δ)) and 0 < r < ρ/(|q| + δ). Flatness of N at x along T makes g vanish on η_{x,r}(M ∩ N). So g = 0 H^n-a.e. on η_{x,r}(M) (restriction evaluated on the open set {g ≠ 0}), and ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} g dH^n = 0.
The defining limit along 𝓝[>] 0 then forces ∫_Q g dH^n = 0, a contradiction. Hence Q ≤ T.

subproblems.title: Projection invariance: an integer multiplicity triple carried by a subspace V is fixed by the orthogonal projection onto V (supplied step 1, q_#T = T)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with orthogonal projection q := V.starProjection, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P (IMRep univ m) whose weight measure μ_R = R.measure = θ·H^m⌞M gives no mass to ℝ^P ∖ V. Then for every m-form ω : ℝ^P → Λ^m(ℝ^P) (no smoothness, support or integrability assumption) R.action(q^#ω) = R.action(ω), where q^#ω = affinePullbackForm q 0 ω, (q^#ω)(x) = ω(0 + q x)∘Λ^m q, and R.action(η) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(η(x)) dH^m(x). (This is q_#τ(M, θ, ξ) = τ(M, θ, ξ), supplied step 1.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), R.measure ((V : Set (Euclid P))ᶜ) = 0 → ∀ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m, R.action (affinePullbackForm V.starProjection 0 ω) = R.action ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the selected node's supplied proof (Simon 7.3.1, footnote 2, chapter-07.txt lines 361–364: spt C ⊆ T_xN), which states that H^m-a.e. x ∈ M has its approximate tangent plane in V and hence Λ_m q ξ(x) = ξ(x). The argument below is that step with the details filled in. It uses the sibling flat_tangent (Submission.atsm_approxTangent_le_of_flat) in place of the supplied 'approximate tangent planes of M and of M ∩ V agree, and a tangent plane of a subset of V lies in V'; flat_tangent states the needed conclusion directly for the set M.
Notation: μ := H^m = μHE[m]; M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult (ℕ-valued, θ ≥ 1 on M), ξ := R.orient; q := V.starProjection; V is a finite-dimensional subspace, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional) and Borel.
1. M ∖ V is H^m-null. By definition R.measure = (μ⌞M).withDensity θ, so by withDensity_apply (Vᶜ is measurable), Measure.restrict_restrict and Set.inter_comm, 0 = R.measure(Vᶜ) = ∫⁻_{Vᶜ} θ d(μ⌞M) = ∫⁻_{M ∩ Vᶜ} θ dμ. Since θ(x) ≥ 1 for x ∈ M (mult_pos), μ(M ∩ Vᶜ) = ∫⁻_{M∩Vᶜ} 1 dμ ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩Vᶜ} θ dμ = 0 (setLIntegral_mono'). Hence μ(M ∖ V) = 0, and consequently μ⌞M-a.e. x lies in V (ae_restrict_iff' with M measurable, together with measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem).
2. Orientation field. By the IMRep field orients, for μ⌞M-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q: there is an orthonormal τ = (τ_1, …, τ_m) with span(τ_1, …, τ_m) = Q such that ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all m-covectors α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α.
3. Approximate tangent planes lie in V. Fix x satisfying both step 1 (x ∈ V) and step 2 (with Q, τ). Apply flat_tangent with N := V (as a set), the set M, the point x, the plane Q and T := V. Its hypotheses hold: (i) H^m(M ∖ V) = 0 by step 1; (ii) V is flat at x along V: given ε > 0 take ρ := 1; for z ∈ V the vector t := z − x lies in V (x, z ∈ V) and ‖z − x − t‖ = 0 ≤ ε‖z − x‖; (iii) HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M x Q by step 2. Hence Q ≤ V. Thus every τ_i ∈ span(τ) = Q ⊆ V, so q τ_i = τ_i, and q x = x since x ∈ V (Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff).
4. Pointwise identity. For x as in step 3 and every m-covector α, (α.compContinuousLinearMap q)(τ_1, …, τ_m) = α(qτ_1, …, qτ_m) = α(τ_1, …, τ_m), so ξ(x)(α∘Λ^m q) = ξ(x)(α) in both sign cases of step 2. Taking α := ω(0 + q x) = ω(x) gives ξ(x)((q^#ω)(x)) = ξ(x)(ω(q x)∘Λ^m q) = ξ(x)(ω(x)), hence θ(x)·ξ(x)((q^#ω)(x)) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)).
5. Conclusion. By steps 1–4 the integrands of R.action(q^#ω) = ∫_M θ·ξ(q^#ω) dμ and R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ·ξ(ω) dμ agree μ⌞M-almost everywhere. Bochner integrals of a.e.-equal functions are equal (integral_congr_ae; this needs no integrability, since both sides are 0 for a non-integrable function), so R.action(q^#ω) = R.action(ω). ∎
Formalization note: this proof was compiled after import GMT.Ch07.Submission, with the flat_tangent statement as a hypothesis; #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
proof_key_steps: θ ≥ 1 on M and μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0 give H^m(M ∖ V) = 0, so H^m⌞M-a.e. x lies in V.
At such x, flat_tangent with N = T = V (flatness is trivial: t = z − x) puts the approximate tangent plane Q of M, oriented by ξ(x) = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τ_m, inside V.
Then qτ_i = τ_i and q x = x, so ξ(x)(ω(q x)∘Λ^m q) = ξ(x)(ω(x)).
The integrands of R.action(q^#ω) and R.action(ω) agree a.e., so the integrals are equal.

subproblems.title: Weight measures of two represented currents agree on an open set where the currents agree (supplied step 5)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let S, T ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) be currents represented by integer multiplicity triples RS and RT in ℝ^P (RS.Represents S, RT.Represents T), and let O ⊆ ℝ^P be open. Suppose S(ω) = T(ω) for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ O. Then the weight measures agree on O: RS.measure⌞O = RT.measure⌞O (Measure.restrict).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (S T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (RS RT : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (O : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen O → RS.Represents S → RT.Represents T → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) ⊆ O → S ω = T ω) → RS.measure.restrict O = RT.measure.restrict O
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the selected node's supplied proof ('S = T on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K', so μ_S = μ_T there'). The supplied proof obtains this from part (c) of im_mass_measure applied in ℝ^P ∖ K' to restricted representations. The argument below uses only the mass formula of the sibling mass_support (Submission.dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support) and the uniqueness of measures on a π-system, which avoids building representations on the smaller domain.
Notation: μ := H^m = μHE[m]; for an IMRep R, R.measure = (μ⌞R.carrier).withDensity R.mult. For a current Z in ℝ^P and a set W, Z.massOn W = sup{ofReal(Z(ω)) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ m W}, where ω is admissible iff ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)|_E ≤ 1 for all x (Simon 6.2.5).
1. Equal masses inside O. Let W ⊆ O. Every admissible ω for W has tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ O, so S(ω) = T(ω) by hypothesis. The two sets {ofReal(S ω)} and {ofReal(T ω)}, indexed by the same admissible forms, therefore coincide (Set.image_congr), and S.massOn W = T.massOn W.
2. Equal measures of open subsets of O. Let W be open with W ⊆ O. By mass_support (with U = ℝ^P open) applied to (S, RS) and to (T, RT): RS.measure(W) = S.massOn W = T.massOn W = RT.measure(W).
3. Local finiteness. For every IMRep R in ℝ^P and every real r: R.measure(B̄(0, r)) = ∫⁻_{R.carrier ∩ B̄(0, r)} θ dμ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict), which is finite by the IMRep field locallyIntegrable_mult applied to the compact set B̄(0, r) ⊆ ℝ^P.
4. Uniqueness. Put μ₁ := RS.measure⌞O and μ₂ := RT.measure⌞O. The open subsets of ℝ^P form a π-system (isPiSystem_isOpen) that generates the Borel σ-algebra, which is the σ-algebra of ℝ^P (BorelSpace.measurable_eq). For every open G, G ∩ O is open and contained in O, so by step 2 μ₁(G) = RS.measure(G ∩ O) = RT.measure(G ∩ O) = μ₂(G) (Measure.restrict_apply, G measurable). The open balls B_i := B(0, i + 1), i ∈ ℕ, belong to the π-system, cover ℝ^P (iUnion_ball_nat_succ), and μ₁(B_i) ≤ RS.measure(B̄(0, i + 1)) < ∞ by step 3. Two measures that agree on a generating π-system containing a countable cover by sets of finite measure are equal (Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion). Hence μ₁ = μ₂. ∎
Formalization note: this proof was compiled after import GMT.Ch07.Submission, with the mass_support statement as a hypothesis; #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
proof_key_steps: Forms admissible for M_W with W ⊆ O give equal values on S and T, so M_W(S) = M_W(T).
By mass_support, RS.measure(W) = RT.measure(W) for every open W ⊆ O.
Both measures are finite on closed balls (locallyIntegrable_mult).
μ⌞O is determined by its values on the π-system of open sets (Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion with the balls B(0, i + 1)).

subproblems.title: Orthogonal projection onto V does not increase mass: M_O(T + q_#X) ≤ μ_{T+X}(q⁻¹(O)) when T is carried by V (supplied step 4)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with orthogonal projection q := V.starProjection, let T, X, S' ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) and let RT, RX be integer multiplicity triples in ℝ^P with RT.Represents T and RX.Represents X. Assume RT.measure(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0, and that K ⊆ ℝ^P is compact with RX.measure(ℝ^P ∖ K) = 0. Assume S'(ω) = T(ω) + RX.action(q^#ω) for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P), where q^#ω = affinePullbackForm q 0 ω. Then there is an integer multiplicity triple R in ℝ^P with R.action(ω) = T(ω) + X(ω) for every test form ω (so R represents every current Z with Z(ω) = T(ω) + X(ω); the contract has no + on currents, and in the parent Z = S = T + (S − T)), and S'.massOn O ≤ R.measure(q⁻¹(O)) for every set O ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (T X S' : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (RT RX : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (K : Set (Euclid P)), RT.Represents T → RX.Represents X → RT.measure ((V : Set (Euclid P))ᶜ) = 0 → IsCompact K → RX.measure Kᶜ = 0 → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, S' ω = T ω + RX.action (affinePullbackForm V.starProjection 0 (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m))) → ∃ R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, R.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) = T ω + X ω) ∧ ∀ O : Set (Euclid P), S'.massOn O ≤ R.measure (V.starProjection ⁻¹' O)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the selected node's supplied proof (projection does not increase mass: |Λ_m q ξ_S(x)| ≤ Π|qτ_i| ≤ 1 by Hadamard's inequality, hence M_{W*}(q_#S) ≤ μ_S(q^{−1}(W*))), together with q_#T = T from its step 1. Here S' = T + q_#X plays the role of q_#S = q_#T + q_#X, and the representation R of T + X (= S) is built so that its action is additive on the non-compactly supported forms q^#ω.
Siblings used: int_combination (Submission.rsdic_exists_imrep_int_combination), projection_invariance (Submission.idtp_fons_cs_sp_action_starProjection_eq), orient_comp (Submission.dtc_bc_lc_pf_unitOrientation_comp) and pairing_bound (Submission.dpf_pfc_imrep_pairing_integrable_abs_le).
Notation: μ := H^m = μHE[m]. For an IMRep R write M_R, θ_R, ξ_R for carrier, mult and orient, and F_R(x) := 1_{M_R}(x)·θ_R(x)·ξ_R(x) ∈ Λ_m(ℝ^P) (R.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R.mult y : ℝ) • R.orient y)). ‖·‖ is the operator norm of a covector or a linear map, |·|_E the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm). q is an orthogonal projection, so ‖q‖ ≤ 1 (starProjection_norm_le); V is closed.
1. Action as a global integral. For every IMRep R and every m-form β, F_R(x)(β(x)) = 1_{M_R}(x)·θ_R(x)·ξ_R(x)(β(x)), so R.action(β) = ∫_{M_R} θ_R ξ_R(β) dμ = ∫ F_R(x)(β(x)) dμ(x) (integral_indicator, M_R measurable). If x ↦ θ_R ξ_R(β) is μ⌞M_R-integrable, then x ↦ F_R(x)(β(x)) is μ-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff).
2. Carriers. If C is measurable and R.measure(Cᶜ) = 0, then μ⌞M_R-a.e. x lies in C. Indeed 0 = R.measure(Cᶜ) = ∫⁻_{M_R ∩ Cᶜ} θ_R dμ (withDensity_apply, restrict_restrict) ≥ μ(M_R ∩ Cᶜ) because θ_R ≥ 1 on M_R; conclude with ae_restrict_iff'.
3. Projected orientation bound. For every IMRep R, for μ⌞M_R-a.e. x and every m-covector α: |ξ_R(x)(α∘Λ^m q)| ≤ |α|_E. Proof: by the field orients, for μ⌞M_R-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_R x) Q, i.e. ξ_R(x) = ±τ_1∧⋯∧τ_m for an orthonormal basis τ of Q. The first part of orient_comp with L := q gives |ξ_R(x)(α∘Λ^m q)| ≤ |α|_E·‖q‖^m (in Simon's terms |⟨α, Λ_m q ξ⟩| = |α(qτ_1, …, qτ_m)| ≤ |α|_E·Π_i|qτ_i|, Hadamard's inequality). Since ‖q‖ ≤ 1 and |α|_E ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg), ‖q‖^m ≤ 1 (pow_le_one₀) and |ξ_R(x)(α∘Λ^m q)| ≤ |α|_E.
4. The combined triple. Apply int_combination with U = ℝ^P (open), R₁ = RT, R₂ = RX and p₁ = p₂ = 1. It gives an IMRep R with F_R = F_RT + F_RX μ-a.e.
5. Additivity. Let β be an m-form such that x ↦ θ_RT ξ_RT(β) is μ⌞M_RT-integrable and x ↦ θ_RX ξ_RX(β) is μ⌞M_RX-integrable. By steps 1 and 4, R.action(β) = ∫ F_R(β) dμ = ∫ (F_RT + F_RX)(β) dμ (integral_congr_ae) = ∫ F_RT(β) dμ + ∫ F_RX(β) dμ (integral_add, integrability from step 1) = RT.action(β) + RX.action(β).
6. Test forms; the first conclusion. Let ω be a test form. It is continuous (hence a.e. strongly measurable for every measure) with compact support C := tsupport ω, hence bounded by some B (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support), and ω(x) = 0 off C (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). So pairing_bound (with U = ℝ^P, F := ω) shows that θ_R ξ_R(ω) is μ⌞M_R-integrable for every IMRep R in ℝ^P. Step 5 gives R.action(ω) = RT.action(ω) + RX.action(ω) = T(ω) + X(ω), since RT represents T and RX represents X.
7. Pull-backs of test forms. Fix a test form ω, let B bound ‖ω‖ and put β := q^#ω, β(x) = ω(0 + q x)∘Λ^m q. Then β is continuous (composition of ω, x ↦ q x and the continuous linear map α ↦ α∘Λ^m q) and ‖β(x)‖ ≤ ‖ω(q x)‖·‖q‖^m ≤ B (ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_compContinuousLinearMap_le, ‖q‖ ≤ 1).
 General principle: let R be an IMRep, D a closed set, C a compact set with R.measure(Dᶜ) = 0 and β(x) = 0 for x ∈ D ∖ C. Then θ_R ξ_R(β) is μ⌞M_R-integrable. Indeed F := 1_D·β is a.e. strongly measurable (β is continuous and D is Borel), vanishes off C (on D ∖ C because β does, and off D by definition), and ‖F(x)‖ ≤ B for all x (B ≥ ‖β(x)‖ ≥ 0, which also covers x ∉ D where F(x) = 0), so pairing_bound gives integrability of θ_R ξ_R(F). By step 2, F = β μ⌞M_R-a.e., so θ_R ξ_R(β) is integrable (Integrable.congr).
 (a) For RX take D = C = K (compact, hence closed); the vanishing condition is empty.
 (b) For RT take D = V and C = V ∩ tsupport ω (compact). If x ∈ V ∖ tsupport ω, then q x = x and ω(q x) = ω(x) = 0, so β(x) = 0.
 Hence step 5 applies to β, and with projection_invariance (applicable because RT.measure(Vᶜ) = 0) R.action(q^#ω) = RT.action(q^#ω) + RX.action(q^#ω) = RT.action(ω) + RX.action(q^#ω) = T(ω) + RX.action(q^#ω) = S'(ω).
8. Mass bound; the second conclusion. Fix O ⊆ ℝ^P. Let ω be admissible for S'.massOn O, i.e. tsupport ω ⊆ O and |ω(y)|_E ≤ 1 for all y, and let β = q^#ω. By step 7, ofReal(S'(ω)) = ofReal(R.action β) ≤ ofReal(|R.action β|) ≤ ∫⁻_{M_R} |θ_R(x)·ξ_R(x)(β(x))| dμ (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm). For μ⌞M_R-a.e. x (step 3):
 - if q x ∈ tsupport ω, then |ξ_R(x)(β(x))| = |ξ_R(x)(ω(q x)∘Λ^m q)| ≤ |ω(q x)|_E ≤ 1;
 - if q x ∉ tsupport ω, then ω(q x) = 0, so β(x) = 0.
 So the integrand is at most θ_R(x)·1_{q⁻¹(tsupport ω)}(x), and ∫⁻_{M_R} θ_R 1_{q⁻¹(tsupport ω)} dμ = R.measure(q⁻¹(tsupport ω)) (lintegral_indicator and withDensity_apply; q⁻¹(tsupport ω) is closed, hence measurable) ≤ R.measure(q⁻¹(O)), since tsupport ω ⊆ O. As S'.massOn O is the supremum of ofReal(S'(ω)) over admissible ω (sSup_le), S'.massOn O ≤ R.measure(q⁻¹(O)). ∎
Formalization note: this proof was compiled after import GMT.Ch07.Submission, with the statements of the four siblings as hypotheses; #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
proof_key_steps: Unit orientations ξ = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τ_m satisfy |ξ(α∘Λ^m q)| ≤ |α|_E·‖q‖^m ≤ |α|_E (orient_comp, ‖q‖ ≤ 1).
int_combination gives R with vector density F_R = F_RT + F_RX a.e., so R.action is additive on forms whose pairings with RT and RX are integrable.

Test forms and the pull-backs q^#ω are integrable against RT and RX (pairing_bound; RT lives on V where q^#ω vanishes off tsupport ω, RX lives on the compact K). Hence R represents T + X and, by projection_invariance, R.action(q^#ω) = S'(ω).
For admissible ω with tsupport ω ⊆ O, |S'(ω)| ≤ ∫_{M_R} θ_R 1_{q⁻¹(tsupport ω)} dH^m = μ_R(q⁻¹(tsupport ω)) ≤ μ_R(q⁻¹(O)).
